rules.telemetry: application/octet-stream only: generated 312-byte little-endian TelemetryBatchHeaderV1 followed by record_count full 5392-byte CycleCaptureRecordV2 records, never JSON/base64. Maximum bytes per batch: 312 + min(ring capacity,4096)*5392 <= 22085944. after is the last consumed sequence; zero starts at sequence 1 with explicit dropped count for overwritten history. Empty batches have first_sequence=0 and last_sequence=after+dropped. Invalid/future cursors return HTTP 409 with catalogue reasons. Streaming flush cadence is 20 ms (unverified off-cycle budget to amortize HTTP overhead while bounding batching latency); one complete batch per write/flush, including empty batches; HTTP intermediaries may reframe chunks. Slow writes terminate at 5 seconds. No session or authority required; transport authentication still applies. Incarnation changes close a stream; reconcile Describe before resetting the cursor.

constraints.axis_mask: Native 32-bit axis mask constrained to the configured group; reset_fault uses zero for all axes.
constraints.binding: controller is 1..63 bytes; pair_id is nonempty; revision nonzero and equal to configured pair revision; configuration_sha256 equals native description.
constraints.fence: Current unpredictable session and exact generation; acquire has no fence; restart fencing takes precedence for dispatched operations.
constraints.handle: Opaque native uint64 identifier, nonzero for start/discard; terminal handles never regain permission.
constraints.identity: start_program requires exact equality with the prepared identity.
constraints.jog: Legacy timeout_ms 1..250; independent jog uses negotiated monotonic host origin, original non-extended deadline and clock incarnation.
constraints.points: 2..250000 points, time_ns int64 nanoseconds; first time zero, increasing subsequent times; position/velocity in described axis order and logical rad/m units; native limits and continuity enforced.

rules.envelope_before_points: Large prepare_trajectory requests must put schema, operation, session and nonzero generation before points within 16384 bytes. Unknown envelope fields and duplicate prefix fields are rejected; full decoding disallows unknown fields. Small unordered bodies fitting the prefix retain existing admission behavior.
rules.errors: The reasons list is the closed catalogue of adapter-owned literal reason labels (including startup/TLS failures). Existing error is also a diagnostic string: JSON, I/O, context, native and dense decoder errors and errors.Join are forwarded unchanged; these open diagnostics are not additional stable reason labels.

events.ordering: Sequences increase within adapter_incarnation. An events_dropped record uses the last lost sequence as its resumable cursor. Retained events keep their original sequences. A future cursor is rejected; adapter restart requires a new cursor.
events.readers: Unix socket filesystem permissions and the existing remote mutual-TLS principal/pair verification apply to both event routes. Events contain no grant session/capability secret.
events.timestamp: time_ns is the daemon publication used to observe a change, not adapter wall time. Native snapshots can coalesce transitions between publications; this stream preserves observations, not every cyclic transition.

rules.recovery: reset_fault is interim: requires inhibited idle native observation, reports correlated reset_sequence, per-bit faults/outcomes and home masks, and retires the session after a submitted result; never starts motion. restore_anchor returns RecoveryStatus from a native publication after the restore receipt, with the restore command sequence in Response.sequence; reset_sequence remains the last fault reset sequence.

remote_jog_upgrade.endpoint: GET /v1/jog on the mutual-TLS listener is exclusively WebSocket upgrade; local GET /v1/jog is the JSON jog_status endpoint.
remote_jog_upgrade.frames: Two calibrate JSON exchanges establish clock bounds before binary local_jog_update frames from protocol/control.json are admitted; successful updates do not get per-update replies. Calibration replies have type, seq, source_ns, host_rx_ns, host_tx_ns; rejection replies have type, seq, reason. With jog_generation=0, send begin with seq=3, axis_mask, a fresh source_ns and the second host_tx_ns after both calibration replies. The server uses the post-calibration Begin sample's earliest host bound as the capture cutoff, independently starts the native first-input allowance at receipt, and replies begun with seq and jog_generation. The native cell age bounds cutoff freshness and the separate wait, and every input retains its original age/deadline checks. Input captured before the Begin source_ns is rejected before clock conversion. Binary input before begin and repeated begin close the stream. Existing nonzero-generation upgrades remain supported. A path session sends begin with "path": true. Binary frames of local_path_samples size carry path chunks (no time); local_jog_update frames with flags bit 0 carry path speed and use the same clock mapping as velocity frames. Each chunk is acknowledged by a path_ack text frame with seq (chunk_sequence) and reason (0 accepted).
remote_jog_upgrade.headers: HTTP/1.1 Connection: Upgrade, Upgrade: websocket, Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13 and a base64 Sec-WebSocket-Key decoding to 16 bytes.

remote_jog_upgrade.response: HTTP 101 upgrades to the dedicated jog lane. Failures before upgrade may be text/plain HTTP 400, 403 or 409; unauthenticated remote requests are denied before the application handler. No Response envelope wraps WebSocket frames.

rules.request_id: Optional on JSON control requests only; 1..64 printable ASCII bytes; null and non-string values rejected. The current session caches 256 outcomes; identical decoded payload retries join/replay, changed payload conflicts; release/expiry detaches the cache.
rules.required_fields: Type.required describes mandatory response/codec fields. Request fields default when omitted; capability.required_fields lists semantically necessary input for valid admission. Native operation-specific defaults and constraints remain authoritative. Codec parsing does not authorize or execute motion.
rules.response: Response.data is the capability response type when named; sequence and handle are envelope fields. Errors return HTTP 409 except body size HTTP 413; success HTTP 200. Native receipts use their existing case-sensitive JSON field names.
rules.external_enable: A6-EC manual chapter 11, 2004h/C04 and 60FDh: bits 16..20 report DI1..DI5 logic; function 1 selects S-ON, function 4 Emergency stop. Wire the cell stop-chain auxiliary contact to a declared DI and configure/read back its function and polarity to observe it. S-ON observation requires exactly one explicit function-1 startup assignment. A dedicated cyclic STO indication is not documented; S-ON/DI observations are diagnostics and never safety certification or a control decision.

control_timing.cell: control.link_profile is lan (500000000/250000000 ns) or internet (unverified 3000000000/750000000 ns). Explicit max_grant_lease_ns and max_jog_input_age_ns override ceilings; unverified absolute bounds 10000000000 and 2000000000 ns. Lease overrides use whole ms. Compiled configuration and native machine identity bind effective nondefault policy.
control_timing.negotiation: Describe publishes max_grant_lease_ns and max_jog_input_age_ns. Acquire requests requested_lease_ms, returns effective lease_ms. Clients size at least three measured round trips plus cadence, capped by cell; renew at most one third of effective lease on a dedicated connection. An insufficient lease fails closed, typed control_session_stale.
control_timing.safety: Longer effective leases increase worst-case unattended-stop delay after operator link loss. Longer input-age ceilings prolong stale velocity application before immutable expiry and the existing jog expiry ramp. Clock uncertainty remains part of worst-case age, never subtracted as network latency.

cell_io.qualification: P6-05: torch remains refused. Generic terminal mappings and cycle bounds are unverified on hardware.
cell_io.fencing: Stop commands OFF in the fence cycle; ON requires a fresh grant, explicit io_arm and valid OFF readback observed after the fence cycle.
cell_io.intent_vs_readback: Intent and commanded values never establish independent physical feedback.
cell_io.marker_collision: Multiple markers for the same output in one native exchange fault; transitions are never silently collapsed.

rules.resources: GET only. Immutable bytes, Content-Length, declared Content-Type and quoted digest ETag. Unknown or malformed digests return resource_unknown with HTTP 404. No repository lookup at request time. Max resource 33554432 bytes, set 134217728 bytes and 1024 entries (unverified bounds).
rules.home_authority: Home is established only by drive homing (HM35), which writes 607C. There is no software current-pose zero; a persisted current-pose (rosie-anchor-v5) anchor is refused as anchor_source_invalid: current-pose reference anchors are not accepted; establish Home with drive homing (HM35).

fields.constraints: Native bus policy and held_slaves with retained, observed and expected declared identities, presence, AL state and disposition; unreadable identity fields are null. Dispositions: held for an undeclared device allowed by hold; declared_unused for a matching declaration; refused_unknown for an undeclared device under refuse; refused_identity for a declared identity mismatch; identity_unreadable for an unavailable SII identity; refused_missing for a missing required declaration; identity_changed for a post-admission identity change under hold; disappeared for a missing unused device under hold; refused_state for a held device outside PREOP or INIT, or a configured terminal outside OP after activation. Refuse continuously requires declared identities and presence; post-admission refusal latches a readiness fault and inhibits outputs before submission, requiring public reset_fault (FaultReset), reacquisition of the application session, then explicit Enable and Arm after restoring the device and verified readiness. Enable before reset is rejected with native not_ready (reason 2); reset clears the readiness fault (reason 128) and safety mask while keeping outputs inhibited and retiring the session. Lost Home evidence requires separate qualified recovery before motion. Hold reports post-admission unused-device identity or presence changes and continues axes while axis readiness remains valid. Admission reason and reason_position identify identity_unreadable, unknown_slave, declared_identity_mismatch, declared_slave_missing, unsafe_held_state or capacity_exceeded; none means no observed refusal. No output capability is granted to held devices. A declared cell I/O terminal has disposition io_terminal and contributes one required responding slave. Its declared identity and presence remain mandatory under both hold and refuse; after activation it must be OP or admission reports io_terminal_not_operational. Held devices alone receive no PDOs or output capability.

fields.name: Active
fields.constraints: True while the servo host's notice file exists and does not say active false; an unreadable or malformed file is active (fails closed) and a notice past its ETA stays active. Exactly the state that refuses acquire and motion starts with busy.

fields.name: Malformed
fields.constraints: The file exists but is not a complete notice (unreadable, not JSON, unknown schema or started_at not RFC 3339); still active.

fields.name: Reason
fields.constraints: The notice's own reason text, trimmed and clipped to 400 bytes; the text a busy refusal wraps. Empty when inactive or when the notice has none.

fields.name: Phase
fields.constraints: The deploy's current step as written, trimmed and clipped to 400 bytes; empty when absent.

fields.name: StartedAt
fields.constraints: RFC 3339 UTC time the notice began; empty when inactive or unparseable.

fields.name: ETA
fields.constraints: RFC 3339 UTC expected end as written by the deploy; empty when absent or unparseable. Informational: passing it never clears the notice.

fields.name: SetBy
fields.constraints: Who or what set the notice, as written, clipped to 400 bytes; empty when absent.

fields.name: Release
fields.constraints: The release or commit being installed, as written, clipped to 400 bytes; empty when absent.

fields.name: Holder
fields.constraints: The current application grant's holder, present whether or not a notice is active; absent while no grant is held. Never carries the session token.

fields.name: Controller
fields.constraints: The caller-chosen acquire controller name (1..63 bytes); a label, not an identity.

fields.name: Remote
fields.constraints: True when the grant was acquired over the mutual-TLS listener; false for the local Unix socket.

fields.name: Identity
fields.constraints: The remote client certificate identity that owns the grant; empty for the local socket.

fields.name: Generation
fields.constraints: The grant's application generation; not a fence on its own without the session.

fields.name: Since
fields.constraints: RFC 3339 UTC time this adapter granted it (adapter wall clock); renewals do not move it.
